subject: Geo guardrails: pin exceptions & subprocessor onboarding for Orion Payments
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request from Orion: strict EU anchoring + temporary analytics window (need proposal)

Team —

Orion Payments (lead: Olivia Chen, DPO) has pushed back on our standard regional failover language. They want a contractual commit to keep production inference and storage anchored to EU regions for EU customers, with one narrow exception: a transient analytics pipeline that may process events in US for up to 48 hours for aggregation before being deleted. They explicitly require:

- A pinned serving config (no automatic cross-region routing for inference) for EU traffic.
- Any transient analytics processing must be auditable, TTL-limited (48h max), and explicitly listed in the DPA as a temporary carveout.
- Full subprocessor roster (cloud infra, telemetry vendors) and gating for future additions.

Can we draft a short operational proposal (optics for legal + security) that covers: the runtime pinning configuration, how KV/cache replication behaves, what audit logs we can provide, and a DPA amendment text for the 48h exception?

Attached: quick region-pin FAQ I sent to Sales earlier.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: region-pin-faq.pdf (summary doc, 3 pages)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request from Orion: strict EU anchoring + temporary analytics window (need proposal)

Diego —

Thanks for the heads up. High-level proposal (for legal + security to review):

1) Operational pin: create a region-binding policy named "orion-eu-anchor" that enforces:
   - All inference requests tagged with customer_id=ORION are routed only to EU clusters (eu-west1, eu-central1).
   - If EU capacity is saturated, requests queue up and trigger escalation to a designated on-call rather than failovering to non-EU.

2) Transient analytics carveout: allow a single outbound export stream that is labeled "orion-analytics" and subject to:
   - Max retention 48 hours enforced at write path.
   - Full access logs emitted with request IDs and origin IPs.
   - No model weights or raw prompt storage exported. Only aggregated telemetry (counts, histograms, anonymized usage metrics).

3) Subprocessor gating: provide current roster and weekly snapshot of changes for 30 days post-signing; any changes that affect EU data handling require 30-day notice + option to terminate.

4) Evidence: include a runbook excerpt showing how KV cache replication is disabled for pinned customers; include forensic audit examples.

I'll draft a one-page "Operational Annex" + a suggested DPA amendment paragraph. Attaching a short checklist I use for these cases.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

---

Subject: Re: Request from Orion: strict EU anchoring + temporary analytics window (need proposal)

FW: technical notes below — forwarding into thread.

On Mon, Oct 11, 2026 at 10:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Diego —
>
> Thanks for the heads up. High-level proposal (for legal + security to review):
>
> 1) Operational pin: create a region-binding policy named \"orion-eu-anchor\" that enforces:
>    - All inference requests tagged with customer_id=ORION are routed only to EU clusters (eu-west1, eu-central1).

My notes:

- Serving runtime: we'll run ORION customers on dedicated pools in the EU tenant (dedicated node groups). This avoids any cross-tenant KV replication.
- Cache/kv: set replication:false for ORION namespace; apply hot-replication only to EU AZs.
- Analytics stream: implement a policy filter on the telemetry pipeline to redact IPs and remove prompt text before any export. We'll also add a TTL hook server-side to expire events after 48h.

Config snippet (pseudo):

route_policy {
  tenant: "ORION"
  region_pin: ["eu-west1","eu-central1"]
  failover: { behavior: "escalate" }
  kv_replication: "eu-only"
  telemetry_export: {
    allowed: true
    export_label: "orion-analytics"
    ttl_hours: 48
    redact_fields: ["prompt_text","user_ip"]
  }
}

I'll work with Infra to estimate the perf/queue behavior if EU pools saturate. Rough ask: give me 48 hours to get a config + ops playbook.

Kimberly
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request from Orion: strict EU anchoring + temporary analytics window (need proposal)

Diego / team —

Legal/regulatory notes from my side:

- DPA amendment: we can add an explicit clause that enumerates the "transient analytics" carveout with a hard TTL (48 hours) and a paragraph stating that data subject requests still apply (we must be able to remove any related records within the TTL window).
- Contract language should require: regular audit logs (30 days retention visible to customer via secure link), notification of subprocessor changes with 30-day notice, and the ability to opt-out if a material subprocessor change occurs.
- For the analytics path, we should specifically enumerate allowed processing types (metrics, anonymized counts) and disallow any raw prompt or model state export.

I can draft the amendment language; however, Olivia will likely ask for evidence. Recommend we bundle: (1) Ops Annex (Marissa), (2) Infra playbook excerpt (Kimberly), and (3) Subprocessor roster CSV.

Soojin
Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Chen <dpo@orionpayments.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: orion-legal@orionpayments.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo guardrails: pin exceptions & subprocessor onboarding for Orion Payments

Diego —

Appreciate the quick coordination. A few clarifying points from our side before we proceed to an amendment: 

1) By "pinned to EU" you mean both inference and any short-term caches remain within EU physical infrastructure? We need a tech proof (network flow diagram) showing that requests from EU customers never egress to US for inference or cache retrieval.

2) The analytics carveout: acceptable provided all of the following are met:
   - TTL enforced at write layer (48 hours, immutable once set).
   - Audit trail for every exported batch (timestamp, records count, export job id).
   - A certified attestation that no raw prompts or PII are exported.

3) Subprocessors: list every subprocessor and their country of processing. We require a dedicated entry in the DPA that any new subprocessor processing EU-origin data triggers a 30-day review with Orion and an option to decline.

Timeline: If Redwood can provide the ops annex + infra diagram + subprocessor roster by EOD Friday (2026-10-16), we'll aim to do a DPO review within 5 business days.

Olivia Chen
DPO, Orion Payments

---
Note: we will need a POC for the audit logs. Please include retention and access controls in the annex.
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-12T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo guardrails: pin exceptions & subprocessor onboarding for Orion Payments

Olivia —

Thanks — understood. Action plan and deliverables: 

1) Ops Annex (Marissa) — outlines region-binding policy, escalation behavior, and audit artifacts. Delivery: 2026-10-16 EOD.
2) Infra diagram + config snippet (Kimberly) — network flow diagram showing EU-only inference paths and cache isolation. Delivery: 2026-10-14 EOD.
3) Subprocessor roster CSV (Diego + Rishi) — complete list with country processing columns and versioned checksum. Delivery: 2026-10-16 EOD.
4) Draft DPA amendment (Soojin) — includes transient-analytics clause, audit log obligations, and subprocessor gating text. Delivery: 2026-10-16 EOD.

We propose a two-week pilot after sign-off to validate instrumentation (audit logs, TTL enforcement) in a staging ribbon in EU before turning on for production. We'll include a PoC path for Orion to query a secure logs endpoint with read-only credentials.

Attaching a short MAP (mutual action plan) for sign-off (see attachment). If acceptable, I'll coordinate a short sync with Olivia & Orion legal next week to walk through evidence.

Best,
Diego
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
